title: Can AI generate all the assets for a game like Final Fantasy Tactics?
author: LargeSinkholesInNYC
selftext: I was thinking that AI can generate all the assets since the units are made of 2d pixels and you barely have any 3D asset in that game.

comments.author: Reign2294
comments.body: I saw an ad/informational on youtube for a website that basically does this. If you're interested, i could try and find it

comments.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
comments.body:
Absolutley.

1. Have AI do concept art that you like.
2. Break it down into sections, tiles, sprites, backgrounds etc.
3. Pixellab is pretty good at that sort of thing, and it can add animations like walking, bending down, jumping etc.

Pixellab can also be used by other AI like Claudecode and Grok etc.

comments.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
comments.body:
If you want more detailed art and 3d assets, basically swap out pixellab for Scenario.

Scenario works differently though. You have to feed it a bunch of concept art so it learns the style you want, and that's actually the hard part, then it can create new assets in that style by vibe coding.

comments.author: Edgezg
comments.body: Smarter option would be to use free assets when available. Generate only what you cannot find for free.

comments.author: GxM42
comments.body: Not if you plan on selling it. AI art in games is basically a product killer. The players review you so badly you can’t recover. Only use it in ways people can’t notice.

comments.author: KeenAsGreen
comments.body:
Yes and it does it fairly well. 
I have had a lot of success doing this with codex. 

Create a sprite sheet generation skill and make sure you have a detailed art-direction.md to keep evrything consistent. 
Then I basically run an agent to generate a required asset list, I then tell codex to generate all the sprite sheets using x skill and following art direction carefully. 
I generated around 5k images yesterday with it and only around 300 failed the review agents pass.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Impress anti ai with your game? No. Otherwise, yes.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
The absolute hardest part is going to be isometric sprites and animations.  GenAI's absolute *weakest* understanding is spatial sense.  Getting it to generate side profiles, or north/south/east/west facing sprites is easy.  Getting it to understand "it's this character, but at a specific consistent pitch and a specific consistent angle.  Now make it face four intercardinal directions" is not something the tech can do reliably via one-shot prompts.

The 3D assets are actually *much easier*, because you're creating a static 3D asset and then letting the game engine's camera handle the angle.

comments.author: TheRealLunicuss
comments.body:
It can but I've found the pixel art generators are rather weak on the isometric front. I'm making a game with FFT inspired combat too. I played around a bunch with a graphics test scene and decided that AI generating art was not going to be feasible. I found it was significantly more time and effort getting the generators to output what I wanted in terms of shape, texture, and most importantly, cohesion with other generated assets.   
  
What was effective is using AI tools to *modify* existing assets: generating subtly different variations of a cobblestone path tile, extrapolating a full sprite sheet worth of different shaped tiles from a single one,  adding texture to a tile (eg. making vines grow out of cracks in the cobblestone), etc etc.
